title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: even if bound when nonexistent — obeyed; ate in Adam not in us
pass_a_gloss: Grant for argument that the ban obligated us while we still were not, Adam alone in paradise with his wife: its demand was simply not to eat that fruit. We kept it—those unable then to eat did not eat. If the reply is that we ate in Adam, then precisely we did not eat in ourselves. Eating in the one Adam fits punishment in the one Adam; not having eaten in our persons, we ought not be punished in our persons.
pass_b_english: But grant that that interdict bound us to obedience for that time when we did not yet exist, when Adam alone was in paradise with his wife—what did it require of us? That we should not eat of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil? We obeyed: for those who at that time could not eat certainly did not eat. We ate, you will say, in Adam. Well and good: therefore we did not eat in ourselves. Since therefore in one Adam we ate that fruit, it was fitting that we also be punished in one Adam: and since we did not eat in our own persons, we ought not to have been punished in our own persons.
source_text: Sed fac interdictum illud nos ad obedientiam obligasse pro eo tempore quo nondum eramus, quo solus erat cum uxore in paradiso Adamus, quid a nobis requirebat? Ut ne ederemus de fructu arboris scientiae boni & mali? Paruimus: nam qui edere tum temporis non poteramus, profecto non edimus. Edimus, inquies, in Adamo. Bene habet: non igitur edimus in nobis. Quandoquidem igitur in uno Adamo manducavimus illum fructum, decuit nos etiam puniri in uno Adamo: ac cum in nostris personis non manducaverimus, non oportuit nos puniri in nostris personis.

choices.choice: Obeyed by inability; ate in Adam not in us; punish in Adam
